reviewedReaderValues.name: Notarial Law

audience.programmeDescription: Leiden’s Notarial Law degree develops a broad foundation in Dutch, European and international law, followed by specialist study of property, family and company law. Students learn to research legal questions, interpret legal sources and build legal arguments.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The supported curriculum totals 125 EC: 120 EC from the revised first two years and a further 5 EC of third-year elective study. The remaining 55 EC of revised third-year study, including the thesis requirements, still need confirmation. The full comparison remains unfinished.

curriculum.limitation: Supported subset: 125 of 180 EC. The revised third-year taught courses and thesis allocation remain under review. The total includes 15 EC of programme electives, with 10 EC in year two and 5 EC in year three, plus a separate 5 EC technology-and-law choice in year two. Mandatory first-year Leiden Law Practices activities, including a passed legal Dutch language test, carry no credits.

componentNotes.not1-01: Alongside the credited first-year courses, students must complete Leiden Law Practices tutoring and pass the legal Dutch language test to complete the first-year examination. These compulsory activities carry 0 EC and do not add to the displayed credits.
componentNotes.not1-06: Builds on Introduction to Private Law I.
componentNotes.not2-01: Entry requires Introduction to Administrative Law; the course builds on its concepts and legal-remedy framework.
componentNotes.not2-02: Entry requires Introduction to Private Law I in the revised curriculum.
componentNotes.not2-03: Entry requires first-year Introduction to European Law.
componentNotes.not2-04: Entry requires Introduction to Private Law I in the revised curriculum.
componentNotes.not2-05: Entry requires both Introduction to Private Law I and II. The course also builds on the law of obligations.
componentNotes.not2-07: Entry requires both Introduction to Private Law I and II. This course excludes marital property law, which is a separate specialist subject.
componentNotes.not2-08: Presupposes a sound understanding of basic obligations and property-law principles.
componentNotes.not2-10: One of three approved 5 EC technology-and-law options. This example uses Philosophy of Technology and Law; students do not take all three for these credits.
componentNotes.not2-11: 10 EC of the programme’s 15 EC elective allowance; the other 5 EC is in year three. Individual elective courses must each carry at least 5 EC. For courses taken within the Law Faculty, the full allowance includes 10 EC at level 200 or above and 5 EC at level 300 or above. Courses must avoid overlap with compulsory study; Honours College courses cannot count. Approval rules apply, with exceptions for recognized minors and Leiden courses meeting the conditions. A 30 EC minor is not automatically counted within this 15 EC allowance.
componentNotes.not3-elective-space-5: The remaining 5 EC of the 15 EC programme elective allowance, placed in year three. The same level, overlap and approval conditions apply as to the second-year elective space. This verified category does not establish the rest of the revised third-year curriculum.
